I ordered this element after ours burnt out and began sparking. Very common occurrence according to Google. Wasn't sure how to compare part models so ordered this based off the fact that it looked like the dysfunctional part currently in our oven. Once it arrived we compared to the old part and it was identical so my husband and I watched a quick YouTube video and set to work. We didn't turn off the power to the oven but were very careful to not allow the wires to fall back behind the oven panel. The one caveat mentioned in the title was the silver, perpendicular pieces at the end of the element that stick up. Our old part had them laying flat. I'm not sure if these were supposed to be bent flat before installation but it quickly became obvious that they weren't going to fit through the slits in the back of the oven without bending them. Fortunately our little adjustment didn't create any issues and the newly installed element works perfectly.

Sears kenmore older model electric stove (25yrs or older) stopped working 12/21. Thought that it may the oven bake element because EVERYTHING ELSE WORKED. Ordered element on 12/22 delivered on 12/23. Great job with super quick delivery. Installed without help except for YouTube.
1. Turned off circuit breaker
2. Didn’t have to pull the stove from the wall (not necessary)
3. Unscrewed element from back of oven pulled the 2 wires out.
4. Because of risk of having wires slip back into the insulation decided to use small clips to prevent that from happening.
5. There was a break on the element that was clearly visible.
6. Tried to just reach to the back to pull and unclip the wires.
7. So I had to take the door off which made the install so much easier.
8. Vacuumed and cleaned out the bottom of oven
9. Reached to the back using both hands and the install took a few minutes.
10. Turned circuit breaker back on and turned oven on and VOILA oven heats up as it should.
11. Trust your ability to do this and save yourself some time and money. As, I did at 70 plus.

Very easy to install. UNPLUG THE RANGE/STOVE BEFORE YOU DO ANYTHING!!! You basically unscrew a couple of screws on each side and gently pull the old heating element out. Before you pull the wires apart off the old element BE CAREFUL and HOLD ON TO the old wires or they WILL kind of get sucked back into the back of the range and behind the insulation. If that happens you have to unscrew the back panel off the entire back of the stove, grab the wire, fish the wire back into the hole so it goes back inside the oven and grab it before it gets sucked back in. How do I know this? Take a guess. Taking the back panel off the stove is easy it just takes more time to take off and push the wire back in then put the back panel back on
